best_for: Busy professionals juggling several Google, Outlook or iCloud calendars plus a task app like Notion or Linear, who want their day time-blocked and are ready to pay for it after a two-week trial.

points.title: No free plan
points.text: Morgen has one plan and a 14-day trial with no credit card. When the trial ends, the account locks until you subscribe. Refunds are offered within 30 days of signing up.

points.title: What it costs
points.text: Pro is USD 30 per month billed monthly, or USD 15 per month billed yearly. Team is USD 25 per seat monthly or USD 10 per seat per month yearly, with at least 2 seats. Students, academics and nonprofits get 25% off Pro. Prices were read on the date below.

points.title: Tasks placed in your calendar
points.text: The Planner suggests which tasks to block out and when, fits them around meetings, and replans when the day changes. It does not change your calendar until you approve.

points.title: Brings your calendars together
points.text: Morgen has no calendar of its own, so you must connect at least one, such as Google Calendar, Outlook or iCloud. Task sources include Notion, Linear, ClickUp and Obsidian. Scheduling links and calendar sets are included.

points.title: Where your data lives
points.text: Morgen says its servers pass calendar data through to your devices without keeping it, unless you opt in to cloud sync for the mobile app or scheduling features.

points.title: Platforms and versions here
points.text: Morgen runs on Mac, Windows, Linux, iOS, Android and the web. This page lists Windows (a per-user x64 installer) and macOS 12 or later for Intel and Apple silicon. The Windows listing keeps 42 versions; macOS only the current release.
